lessons.title: Powers of 10 & Place Value Shifts
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Multiplying by Powers of 10
lessons.reading: An exponent on 10 tells how many times 10 is multiplied by itself. For example, 10² = 100 (2 zeros) and 10³ = 1,000 (3 zeros). To multiply a whole number by 10ⁿ, shift the digits n places to the left.

principles.title: Multiplying by Powers of 10
principles.summary: Use exponents to represent powers of 10 and shift place values accurately.

lessons.title: Rounding, Adding & Subtracting Decimals
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Rounding, Adding & Subtracting Decimals
lessons.reading: To round a decimal to the nearest tenth, check the hundredths digit (5 or more rounds up). When adding or subtracting decimals, line up the decimal points vertically so tenths add to tenths.

principles.title: Adding and Subtracting Decimals to Tenths
principles.summary: Line up decimal points vertically to add and subtract decimals.

lessons.reading: Use the standard algorithm to multiply 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers by adding partial products. For division by a 2-digit divisor, use inverse multiplication to find the exact quotient.

lessons.title: Multiplying Fractions & Dividing by Unit Fractions
lessons.reading: To multiply two fractions, multiply the numerators together and multiply the denominators together. To divide a whole number by a unit fraction (such as 4 ÷ 1/3), count how many 1/3 pieces fit in 4 wholes: 4 × 3 = 12.

principles.title: Multiplying Fractions

lessons.title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
lessons.reading: Volume measures the 3-D space inside a solid figure in cubic units. For any rectangular prism, multiply length × width × height (V = l × w × h).

principles.title: Volume of a Rectangular Prism
